review_notes: Reviewed the full 67-line target and the imported finite-disk collar, endpoint-neighborhood, and polygonal-replacement declarations. The only supported generalization I found is to require finiteness of the index type without fixing a particular Fintype instance.

findings.problem: The theorem requires both an explicit enumeration instance and decidable equality, although its conclusion and geometric hypotheses depend only on the index type being finite. This excludes callers who know only `[Finite ι]` and needlessly exposes instance choices in the theorem interface.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the header with `{ι : Type*} [Finite ι]` and begin the proof with `classical` and `letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι`; the remaining proof can use the resulting instances when invoking `exists_finite_disk_collar`.
findings.benefit: The theorem becomes applicable to any propositionally finite index type without callers constructing or passing a particular Fintype or DecidableEq instance. The finiteness condition remains, so the finite-intersection argument and degenerate finite index cases are preserved.
